newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's preliminary Oct trade surplus $277 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's preliminary Oct trade surplus $277 mln.

text.p: Mexico's preliminary trade surplus was $277 million in October, on exports of $9.226 billion and imports of $8.949 billion, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.

It said both exports and imports were at 1996 record highs, partly because of the numbers of working days in October and also because of a surge in imports of consumer goods ahead of year-end. The balance was lower than the $435.93 million surplus forecast in a Reuters survey.

Manufacturing exports in October were $7.793 billion, up 19.2 percent from the same month last year. Maquiladora, or in-bond industry, exports rose 23.9 percent over the same period, while non-maquiladora exports were up 15.2 percent.
Sales abroad of petroleum products surged 105.8 percent from October 1995, to $1.227 billion. Agricultural exports were $168 million and mining accounted for $38 million.
The $8.949 billion import bill was 35 percent higher than October 1995 and more than $1 billion above the $7.87 billion average Reuters forecast.
The Finance Ministry said a 50.5 percent surge in consumer goods imports to $704 million in October reflected a recovery in consumer spending as well as pre-Christmas purchases.
Intermediate goods imports rose 31.8 percent to $7.185 billion in October and purchases of capital goods were up 49.6 percent to $1.060 billion.
